rule: A ring homomorphism preserves subtraction, followed by the definition of its kernel

conditions.justification: This is the explicit hypothesis and implies phi(a-b)=phi(a)-phi(b).

conditions.condition: phi(a)=0 and phi(b)=0 for the chosen a,b in ker(phi).
conditions.justification: Both equalities were established in the preceding node from kernel membership.

circularity.justification: The calculation uses only homomorphism properties and the prior kernel-membership equalities.

conclusion.statement: We have phi(a - b) = phi(a) - phi(b) = 0, so a - b is in ker(phi).
conclusion.justification: Homomorphicity gives phi(a-b)=phi(a)-phi(b)=0-0=0, and the definition of the kernel then gives a-b in ker(phi).

reason: The subtraction calculation and its kernel conclusion are correct in arbitrary associative rings.
